    19	*medallion* has been designed to be a simple front-end REST server providing
    20	access to the endpoints defined in that specification.
    21	It uses the python framework - `Flask <http://flask.pocoo.org/>`_.  *medallion*
    22	depends on back-end "plugins" which handle the persistence of the TAXII data and
    23	metadata. The TAXII specification is agnostic to what type of data a TAXII
    24	server stores, but this will usually be STIX 2 content.
    25	
    26	Two back-end plugins are provided with *medallion*: the Memory back-end and the
    27	MongoDB back-end.  The Memory back-end persists data "in memory".  It is
    28	initialized using a json file that contains TAXII data and metadata.
    29	It is possible to save the current state of the in memory store, but this
    30	back-end is really intended only for testing purposes.  The MongoDB backend is
    31	somewhat more robust and makes use of a MongoDB server, installed independently.
    32	The MongoDB back-end can only be used if the pymongo python package is
    33	installed. An error message will result if it is used without that package.
    34	
    35	
    36	Installation
    37	============
    38	
    39	The easiest way to install *medallion* is with pip::
    40	
    41	  $ pip install medallion
    42	
    43	
    44	Usage
    45	=====
    46	
    47	As a script
    48	-----------
    49	
    50	Medallion provides a command-line interface to start the TAXII Server::
    51	
    52	    usage: medallion [-h] [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--debug-mode]
    53	                  [--log-level {DEBUG,INFO,WARN,ERROR,CRITICAL}]
    54	                  CONFIG_PATH
    55	
    56	    medallion v0.2.1
    57	
    58	    positional arguments:
    59	      CONFIG_PATH           The location of the JSON configuration file to use.
    60	
    61	    optional arguments:
    62	      -h, --help            show this help message and exit
    63	
    64	      --host HOST           The host to listen on.
    65	
    66	      --port PORT           The port of the web server.
    67	
    68	      --debug-mode          If set, start application in debug mode.
    69	
    70	      --log-level {DEBUG,INFO,WARN,ERROR,CRITICAL}
    71	                            The logging output level for medallion.
    72	
    73	To run *medallion*::
    74	
    75	    $ python medallion/scripts/run.py <config-file>
    76	
    77	The <config_file> contains:
    78	
    79	- configuration information for the backend plugin
    80	- a simple user name/password dictionary
    81	
    82	To use the Memory back-end plug, include the following in the <config-file>:
    83	
    84	.. code:: python
    85	
    86	    {
    87	        "backend": {
    88	            "module": "medallion.backends.memory_backend",
    89	            "module_class": "MemoryBackend",
    90	            "filename": <path to json file with initial data>
    91	        }
    92	    }
    93	
    94	To use the Mongo DB back-end plug, include the following in the <config-file>:
    95	
    96	.. code:: python
    97	
    98	    {
    99	         "backend": {
   100	            "module": "medallion.backends.mongodb_backend",
   101	            "module_class": "MongoBackend",
   102	            "uri": <Mongo DB server url>  # e.g., "mongodb://localhost:27017/"
   103	         }
   104	    }
   105	
   106	*Note: A Mongo DB should be available at some URL when using the Mongo DB back-end*
   107	
   108	A description of the Mongo DB structure expected by the mongo db backend code is
   109	described in `the documentation
   110	<https://medallion.readthedocs.io/en/latest/mongodb_schema.html>`_.
   111	
   112	As required by the TAXII specification, *medallion* supports HTTP Basic
   113	authorization.  However, the user names and passwords are currently stored in
   114	the <config_file> in plain text.
   115	
   116	Here is an example:
   117	
   118	.. code:: python
   119	
   120	    {
   121	        "users": {
   122	           "admin": "Password0",
   123	           "user1": "Password1",
   124	           "user2": "Password2"
   125	        }
   126	    }
   127	
   128	The authorization is enabled using the python package
   129	`flask_httpauth <https://flask-httpauth.readthedocs.io>`_.
   130	Authorization could be enhanced by changing the method "decorated" using
   131	@auth.get_password in medallion/__init__.py
   132	
   133	We welcome contributions for other back-end plugins.
   134	
   135	Docker
   136	======
   137	
   138	We also provide a Docker image to make it easier to run *medallion*::
   139	
   140	    $ docker build . -t medallion
   141	
   142	If operating behind a proxy, add the following option (replacing `<proxy>` with
   143	your proxy location and port): ``--build-arg https_proxy=<proxy>``.
   144	
   145	Then run the image::
   146	
   147	    $ docker run --rm -p 5000:5000 -v <directory>:/var/taxii medallion
   148	
   149	Replace ``<directory>`` with the full path to the directory containing your
   150	medallion configuration.

     5	Spans is a pure Python implementation of PostgreSQL's

    27	Example
    28	-------
    29	Imagine you are building a calendar and want to display all weeks that overlaps
    30	the current month. Normally you have to do some date trickery to achieve this,
    31	since the month's bounds may be any day of the week. With Spans' set-like
    32	operations and shortcuts the problem becomes a breeze.
    33	
    34	We start by importing ``date`` and ``daterange``
    35	
    36	.. code-block:: python
    37	
    38	    >>> from datetime import date
    39	    >>> from spans import daterange
    40	
    41	Using ``daterange.from_month`` we can get range representing January in the year
    42	2000
    43	
    44	.. code-block:: python
    45	
    46	    >>> month = daterange.from_month(2000, 1)
    47	    >>> month
    48	    daterange(datetime.date(2000, 1, 1), datetime.date(2000, 2, 1))
    49	
    50	Now we can calculate the ranges for the weeks where the first and last day of
    51	month are
    52	
    53	.. code-block:: python
    54	
    55	    >>> start_week = daterange.from_date(month.lower, period="week")
    56	    >>> end_week = daterange.from_date(month.last, period="week")
    57	    >>> start_week
    58	    daterange(datetime.date(1999, 12, 27), datetime.date(2000, 1, 3))
    59	    >>> end_week
    60	    daterange(datetime.date(2000, 1, 31), datetime.date(2000, 2, 7))
    61	
    62	Using a union we can express the calendar view.
    63	
    64	.. code-block:: python
    65	
    66	    >>> start_week.union(month).union(end_week)
    67	    daterange(datetime.date(1999, 12, 27), datetime.date(2000, 2, 7))

        # Special case for empty ranges
        if not self or not other:

        sl = self._lower_bound
        su = self._upper_bound
        ol = other._lower_bound
        ou = other._upper_bound

"""

from spans import floatrange, intrange

def test_existing_intersection_behavior():
    """Test that existing intersection behaviors still work."""
    
    print("=== Regression Testing Existing Behavior ===")
    
    # Test cases from the existing test suite
    test_cases = [
        # (range1, range2, expected_intersection)
        (intrange(1, 5), intrange(1, 5), intrange(1, 5)),
        (intrange(1, 15), intrange(5, 10), intrange(5, 10)),
        (intrange(1, 5), intrange(3, 8), intrange(3, 5)),
        (intrange(3, 8), intrange(1, 5), intrange(3, 5)),
        (intrange(3, 8, lower_inc=False), intrange(1, 5), intrange(3, 5, lower_inc=False)),
        (intrange(1, 10), intrange(5), intrange(5, 10)),
        (intrange(1, 10), intrange(upper=5), intrange(1, 5)),
    ]
    
    for i, (r1, r2, expected) in enumerate(test_cases):
        result = r1.intersection(r2)
        print(f"Test {i+1}: {r1} ∩ {r2} = {result}")
        assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    print("✅ All existing intersection behaviors preserved")

def test_float_specific_intersections():
    """Test float-specific intersection cases."""
    
    print("\n=== Float-Specific Intersection Testing ===")
    
    # Normal overlaps
    r1 = floatrange(1.0, 5.0)
    r2 = floatrange(3.0, 8.0)
    result = r1.intersection(r2)
    expected = floatrange(3.0, 5.0)
    print(f"Normal overlap: {r1} ∩ {r2} = {result}")
    assert result == expected
    
    # Complete containment
    r1 = floatrange(1.0, 10.0)
    r2 = floatrange(3.0, 8.0)
    result = r1.intersection(r2)
    expected = floatrange(3.0, 8.0)
    print(f"Containment: {r1} ∩ {r2} = {result}")
    assert result == expected
    
    # Point intersection (both inclusive at boundary)
    r1 = floatrange(1.0, 5.0, upper_inc=True)
    r2 = floatrange(5.0, 10.0, lower_inc=True)
    result = r1.intersection(r2)
    expected = floatrange(5.0, 5.0, lower_inc=True, upper_inc=True)
    print(f"Point intersection: {r1} ∩ {r2} = {result}")
    assert result == expected
    
    # No intersection cases
    r1 = floatrange(1.0, 5.0)
    r2 = floatrange(6.0, 10.0)
    result = r1.intersection(r2)
    print(f"No overlap: {r1} ∩ {r2} = {result}")
    assert not result  # Should be empty
    
    print("✅ All float-specific cases work correctly")

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Unit test for URL decoding functionality in _normalize_hosts
"""

import unittest
from elasticsearch.client import _normalize_hosts


class TestUrlDecode(unittest.TestCase):
    
    def test_username_with_special_chars_is_decoded(self):
        """Test that usernames with URL-encoded special characters are properly decoded."""
        test_url = "http://user%5D:password@example.com:9200/"
        result = _normalize_hosts([test_url])
        self.assertEqual(result[0]['http_auth'], 'user]:password')
        
    def test_password_with_special_chars_is_decoded(self):
        """Test that passwords with URL-encoded special characters are properly decoded.""" 
        test_url = "http://username:pass%5D@example.com:9200/"
        result = _normalize_hosts([test_url])
        self.assertEqual(result[0]['http_auth'], 'username:pass]')
        
    def test_both_username_and_password_with_special_chars_are_decoded(self):
        """Test that both username and password with special chars are decoded."""
        test_url = "http://user%5B%5D:pass%5B%5D@example.com:9200/"
        result = _normalize_hosts([test_url])
        self.assertEqual(result[0]['http_auth'], 'user[]:pass[]')
        
    def test_normal_credentials_still_work(self):
        """Test that normal (non-encoded) credentials still work."""
        test_url = "http://user:pass@example.com:9200/"
        result = _normalize_hosts([test_url])
        self.assertEqual(result[0]['http_auth'], 'user:pass')
        
    def test_mixed_encoded_and_normal_credentials(self):
        """Test mix of encoded and normal credentials."""
        test_url = "http://user%40domain:pass@example.com:9200/"
        result = _normalize_hosts([test_url])
        self.assertEqual(result[0]['http_auth'], 'user@domain:pass')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
